claims.head: Like for like: McCann against McKenna
claims.call: The Kraken’s L3 (Wright, Catton and McCann) spends at least 49% of its 5-on-5 time against the Maple Leafs’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Kraken keep sending McCann’s line (Wright, Catton and McCann) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Lane Lambert keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Maple Leafs’ third line is McKenna, Sissons and Lettieri.
claims.nums: At home: 49% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 28% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Lane Lambert likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Maple Leafs’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Seattle home games this season · 5 games, 41 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Seattle’s L3 (Wright, Catton and McCann) at home: 49% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, Seattle home games this season, 5 games, 41 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 28% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

check.measure: share of Seattle L3's 5-on-5 time against Toronto L3
check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Maple Leafs’ power play has a target
claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ power play creates at least their usual 8.2 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most.

claims.head: Shots should fly both ways
claims.call: The game’s pace score is above 104, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.see: More than 69 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 56 or more shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Kraken. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: The Kraken roll four lines, the Maple Leafs lean on their top six
claims.body: On depth, Seattle is one of the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Kraken.

notes.text: Chris Tanev is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Darren Raddysh has taken his spot beside Jake McCabe.
Kirill Marchenko is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Dakota Mermis has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Vinni Lettieri was added to the roster on Oct 19 and has played beside Colton Sissons and Gavin McKenna.
Dakota Mermis was added to the roster on Oct 24.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 6% last season.
Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Cale Fleury returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 45% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 2% last season.

SEA.head: Leaning the Kraken’s way
SEA.body: Seattle has home-ice advantage, while Toronto will be without Marchenko. Then again, Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately, and Seattle will be without McCann. Still, it’s close: the Maple Leafs can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs start a half-step behind
TOR.body: Seattle has home-ice advantage, while Toronto will be without Marchenko. Then again, Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately, and Seattle will be without McCann. The Maple Leafs’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

story.head: McMann meets his old team
paras: The Maple Leafs come in at 7-5-2, the Kraken at 7-4-1.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Maple Leafs’ third line. The Leafs’ power play has a soft target in the Kraken’s kill.

items.text: Bobby McMann faces Toronto for the first time since leaving.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko and Nick Blankenburg, and have been without Chris Tanev and John Tavares for several games.
The Kraken are newly without Jared McCann.
Morgan Rielly is two goals from 100.
